jobs.title: Director of Community Engagement, Alpha - $400,000/year USD
jobs.description:
Families who enroll at Alpha rarely arrive because of an advertisement. They come because someone they trust—another parent, across the table at dinner—told them, "This transformed my child." You would be responsible for that word-of-mouth engine across an entire region: orchestrating the dinners, cultivating parent ambassadors, engaging the mayor's office, connecting the CEO who gives a 14-year-old their first meaningful project.

In a typical week, you will be present in four different rooms. You design and execute the regional event calendar—gatherings that range from 150-person open houses to eight-seat curated dinners, several times each month. You identify and prepare current parents who are eager to speak with prospective families, then facilitate those family-to-family connections. You cultivate ties with civic leaders and corporate executives, converting those relationships into event venues, allies for campus expansions, and tangible opportunities for students. And you deliver the Alpha Networks promise: introductions, expert-led masterclasses, internships, alumni integration—tracked and fulfilled family by family.

There is no complete playbook waiting for you. You will build it as you execute, and the frameworks you create will be adopted by colleagues running parallel efforts in other markets. As your region expands, the performance bar rises rather than drops: doors opened per family must increase even as total enrollment grows. Success is measured by the proportion of new families who arrive through genuine personal endorsements, tracked over years rather than quarters.

No specific degree or institutional background is required. An MBA, a career in consulting or wealth management, or a track record built through community work, hospitality, or institutional advancement all carry equal weight. What matters is your demonstrated ability to convene people and convert those relationships into measurable outcomes.

This position is based on-site in one of the following regions: San Francisco, Los Angeles, San Diego, Denver, Greenwich, Miami, Atlanta, Boston, Oklahoma City, Tulsa, Dorado, Nashville, or Park City. The role involves evening and weekend engagements with high-expectation parents, elected officials, and entrepreneurs, along with consistent local travel. You will become the most connected individual in your city, and you will direct that capital toward children. If that exchange feels like the purpose rather than a burden, you should apply.

What You Will Be Doing

Creating and executing the regional event calendar: open events, curated dinners segmented by city and grade level, and family retreats—multiple events monthly, within budget
Identifying and securing venues, hosts, and vendors, then serving as the live host for each event
Identifying and training current parents to serve as ambassadors, arming them with authentic narratives, and pairing them with prospective families and campus tours
Establishing connections with government officials and corporate leaders, and converting those into event venues, support for new campus launches, and opportunities for students
Facilitating enrollment of families into parent circles and placement of students into mentorships, masterclasses, and professional internships; welcoming graduating families into the alumni network within 30 days
Recording every event, introduction, and first-contact source in the CRM to ensure "doors opened per family" is an accurate, verifiable metric

What You Won’t Be Doing

Purchasing growth. No paid advertising, no ad budgets, no targets based on impressions or lead volume
Controlling the brand narrative or executing top-down campaigns; that belongs to Marketing
Handling admissions processing, conducting tours, or managing enrollment documentation; Admissions and Family Success own those functions
Managing day-to-day campus operations or opening physical facilities
Treating raw attendance or headcount as if a full room alone constitutes success
Waiting for a complete playbook, templates, or dedicated support staff before taking action

Director Of Community Engagement Key Responsibilities

Drive people-first referrals to become the primary source of enrollment growth in your region.

Basic Requirements

5+ years building communities or relationship-driven programs in K-12 education, membership organizations, or comparable network businesses where growth originated from people: referrals, members, congregations, chapters, alumni, or client portfolios, with quantifiable results
Personal experience designing and executing 20+ events spanning the full spectrum, from intimate curated dinners to open events with 100+ attendees, including budget responsibility
Established and sustained relationships with government officials or corporate executives that delivered concrete, identifiable outcomes
Disciplined CRM practitioner; tracking relationships, attributions, and actions is already standard practice for you
Currently resides in, or willing to relocate to, one of these regions: San Francisco, Los Angeles, San Diego, Denver, Greenwich (CT), Miami, Atlanta, Boston, Oklahoma City, Tulsa, Dorado (PR), Nashville, or Park City (UT)
Authorized to work in the US without requiring visa sponsorship

Nice-to-have Requirements

Led regional growth, community, or partnership functions for a network-based organization: a school network, membership club, franchise system, or civic or faith-based institution
Developed and monetized a high-trust portfolio of relationships as a client-facing principal in wealth management, consulting, or business development
Advanced through admissions, institutional advancement, community organizing, or hospitality, and were consistently selected to host and represent the organization
Pre-existing relationships with local government or the business community in your target city
Deep understanding of how families evaluate and make high-stakes education decisions

About Alpha

Join the team building school around student growth

Alpha reimagines the school day around faster learning, stronger mentorship, and more time for students to build real-world skills.

Roles with real student impact:
Alpha hires teachers (guides), operators, admissions experts, school & curriculum leaders, and remote team members.

Education work that pays like it matters:
Alpha offers six-figure roles for people ready to help build a radically better school experience.

A culture built for builders:
Alpha is fast-moving, ambitious, and student focused. It’s for people who want to improve the system, not maintain it.

Alpha is where you can do the most meaningful work of your career.

There is so much to cover for this exciting role, and space here is limited. Hit the Apply button if you found this interesting and want to learn more. We look forward to meeting you!

The compensation level for this role is $400,000 USD/year. The payment period is weekly. Consult www.crossover.com/help-and-faqs for more details on this topic.

jobs.title: Director of Strategic Partnerships - North America
jobs.description:
Tencent Games was established in 2003. We are a leading global platform for game development, operations and publishing, and the largest online game community in China. Tencent Games has developed and operated over 140 games. We provide cross-platform interactive entertainment experience for more than 800 million users in over 200 countries and regions around the world. Honor of Kings, PUBG MOBILE, and League of Legends, are some of our most popular titles around the world. Meanwhile, we actively promote the development of esports industry, work with global partners to build an open, collaborative and symbiotic industrial ecology, and create high-quality digital life experiences for players.

About the Role

Tencent Games is looking for a senior partnerships leader to own and deepen our relationships with the most important companies in Western gaming — first-party platforms, major publishers, and leading developers. This is a relationship-first role for someone who can open doors at the executive level, turn conversations into long-term strategic partnerships, and represent Tencent credibly with the industry's most senior decision-makers.

What You'll Do

Own senior-level relationships with key platform and publisher partners, serving as a trusted point of contact from working teams up to the C-suite
Identify, shape, and drive strategic partnership opportunities end-to-end — from first conversation through structuring, alignment, and execution
Partner closely with business unit leadership and cross-functional teams (studios, publishing, investment, legal) to land and deliver on partnership commitments
Bring sharp, timely market and competitive intelligence back into the organization to inform strategy and deal priorities
Represent Tencent Games at major industry events, conferences, and executive forums

Who We Look For

Based in North America with 10+ years in gaming, or in consulting/banking with deep gaming sector exposure
An existing network across platforms and publishers — established C-suite and senior executive relationships are a strong plus
A natural relationship builder who thrives on opening new doors: comfortable cold-calling a studio founder on Monday and presenting to a platform executive on Friday
Equally strong as a team player and an independent operator — you don't wait to be handed opportunities
Outstanding communication, analytical, and interpersonal skills; comfortable with ambiguity and matrixed organizations
Genuine passion for games and the business behind them

The expected base pay range for this position in the location(s) listed above is $147,400.00 to $303,600.00 per year. Actual pay may vary depending on job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. Employees hired for this position may be eligible for a sign on payment, relocation package, and restricted stock units, which will be evaluated on a case-by-case basis. Subject to the terms and conditions of the plans in effect, hired applicants are also eligible for medical, dental, vision, life and disability benefits, and participation in the Company’s 401(k) plan. The Employee is also eligible for up to 15 to 25 days of vacation per year (depending on the employee’s tenure), up to 13 days of holidays throughout the calendar year, and up to 10 days of paid sick leave per year. Your benefits may be adjusted to reflect your location, employment status, duration of employment with the company, and position level. Benefits may also be pro-rated for those who start working during the calendar year.

Equal Employment Opportunity at Tencent

As an equal opportunity employer, we firmly believe that diverse voices fuel our innovation and allow us to better serve our users and the community. We foster an environment where every employee of Tencent feels supported and inspired to achieve individual and common goals.

jobs.title: Youth Development Director, Alpha - $200,000/year USD
jobs.description:
On-site at an Alpha campus in Miami, FL, or New York City, NY — relocation assistance available
$200,000/year
Full-time

Most schools lower expectations when students fall behind. You take a different approach.

You know young children can achieve far more than traditional classrooms demand, and you've led teams that demonstrate this through concrete, measurable outcomes. You understand that accountability, motivation, and rigorous standards transform lives in ways that no worksheet can replicate.

Alpha dedicates just two hours each morning to academics through adaptive learning technology. This structure allows you to concentrate on the work with the greatest lasting impact: coaching students toward independent learning and developing the Guides who enable that progress. You will lead outcomes for a cohort of K-3 students, applying data, observation, and coaching to ensure each child loves school, learns twice as fast, and builds exceptional life skills.

This position is neither an instructional coach role nor a principal role. You won't be consumed by meetings or administrative tasks. Instead, you'll be present in classrooms, evaluating student and Guide performance, running workshops on focus, resilience, communication, and accountability, and coaching children and adults toward quantifiable progress.

Your impact will extend beyond your immediate cohort. You'll capture effective practices, create playbooks that elevate standards schoolwide, and contribute to how Alpha trains future Guides. If building people, scaling excellence, and proving that exceptional outcomes are achievable when expectations remain high energizes you, we want to hear from you.

What You Will Be Doing

Use performance data, classroom observations, and direct feedback to coach Guides and students toward measurable gains.
Run engaging workshops for K-3 students that develop communication, resilience, collaboration, accountability, focus, and other essential life skills.
Conduct one-on-one and small-group coaching sessions that link student motivation to academic achievement and self-sufficiency.
Create and improve repeatable coaching playbooks that strengthen performance across the Guide team.
Train and mentor Guides while demonstrating exceptional coaching and facilitation practices daily.

What You Won’t Be Doing

Teaching traditional classroom lessons or presenting academic content through lectures; adaptive technology manages core academics.
Using punishment to manage discipline or reducing expectations when students face difficulties.
Operating from an office rather than engaging directly with students and Guides each day.
Managing campus operations, budgets, or parent communications; your priority is people development and outcome improvement.
Adhering to conventional elementary school methods simply because "that's how it's always been done."

Youth Development Director Key Responsibilities

Fulfill Alpha's three promises for every K-3 student by developing high-performing Guides, highly motivated students, and a coaching culture that reliably produces outstanding academic and life outcomes.

Basic Requirements

Willing to work on-site at an Alpha campus in Miami, FL or New York City, NY; relocation assistance is provided
Bachelor's degree in Education, Psychology, Business, Organizational Leadership, Child Development, or a related field.
At least 5 years of experience working with elementary-aged children (approximately ages 5-9).
Experience leading teams of five or more people, including performance management and hiring decisions.
Experience building, launching, or significantly growing a program, school, team, or initiative rather than maintaining an existing one.
Demonstrated success using data and measurable outcomes to improve team or student performance.
Excited by challenging conventional education models and embracing a coaching-first approach.
Legally authorized to work in the United States.

Nice-to-have Requirements

Master's degree in a related field.
Experience using dashboards, analytics, or performance metrics to drive continuous improvement.
Track record of coaching adults toward measurable performance outcomes.
Background in youth development, competitive coaching, enrichment programs, camps, or other high-accountability environments.
Strong public speaking and facilitation skills with young children.

jobs.title: Solar Business Development Director
jobs.description:
About Montante Solar

From community solar portfolios to commercial rooftops, battery storage, schools and government projects, Montante solar delivers energy solutions built around real-world needs. With experience across every phase of a project, our team guides development, engineering, procurement, construction, and O & M to ensure each system performs reliably and efficiently.

Role Overview

The Business Development Director is a senior growth leader responsible for expanding Montante Solar's customer and partner relationships, originating high-quality solar and energy storage opportunities, and strengthening the company's position as a leading distributed energy contractor and partner.

New York will remain Montante Solar's primary market and the central focus of this role. The Director will also help expand the company's relationships and project pipeline in targeted growth markets, including Pennsylvania and Illinois, while identifying select opportunities in other attractive U.S. markets where Montante Solar's capabilities, relationships, and experience provide a competitive advantage.

A particular focus will be developing and expanding long-term relationships with IPPs, developers, asset owners, and other strategic partners capable of generating repeat EPC, development, and O&M opportunities.

The successful candidate will combine strong business development and relationship management skills with renewable energy industry experience, an established professional network, and the ability to develop new markets and strategic partnerships.

Success will be measured not only by closed sales, but by the quality and depth of relationships developed, growth of the qualified opportunity pipeline, expansion of repeat business, successful entry into targeted markets, collaboration with internal teams, and the overall customer experience.

Impact

The Business Development Director will play a key role in Montante Solar's next phase of growth by expanding our distributed solar and energy storage pipeline, strengthening relationships with existing customers and development partners, and establishing new strategic relationships.

The Director will deepen Montante Solar's presence throughout New York while helping build a repeatable pipeline of opportunities in targeted growth markets such as Pennsylvania and Illinois. The Director will also help identify other markets where customer relationships, developer partnerships, market conditions, or Montante Solar's capabilities create a compelling opportunity for expansion.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Partnerships & Market Expansion

Develop and expand relationships with IPPs, solar and energy storage developers, asset owners, investors, and other strategic partners capable of generating repeat project opportunities.
Position Montante Solar as a preferred EPC and long-term partner to developers and IPPs operating within New York and targeted growth markets.
Expand Montante Solar's relationships and project pipeline throughout New York, which will remain the company's primary market
Help develop and execute market-entry strategies for targeted growth markets, initially including Pennsylvania and Illinois
Identify additional geographic markets where customer relationships, developer partnerships, project economics, or market conditions create attractive opportunities for Montante Solar.
Develop relationships that create recurring EPC, development, and O&M opportunities rather than solely transactional, project-by-project sales.
Provide market intelligence to company leadership regarding competitors, customers, developers, regulatory conditions, and emerging opportunities that may influence Montante Solar's growth strategy.

Business Development & Relationship Management

Own and manage an active pipeline of qualified opportunities while maintaining accurate forecasting and next-step accountability.
Develop and maintain relationships with commercial, industrial, municipal, educational, and institutional customers.
Identify, qualify, and advance distributed solar and energy storage opportunities.
Generate new business opportunities through networking, referrals, strategic outreach, industry associations, and marketing initiatives.
Coordinate with Marketing on campaigns, trade shows, customer communications and thought leadership.
Identify customer success stories and market insights that strengthen the Montante Solar brand.
Represent Montante Solar at industry events, conferences, trade associations, and community organizations.
Maintain a strong network of relationships with developers, property owners, brokers, consultants, engineers, utilities, and industry stakeholders.

Business Development Operations

Ensure Sugar CRM serves as the central repository for all business development activities.
Lead the BD pipeline review and forecasting process
Ensure opportunities, contacts, next steps and forecasts remain current.
Develop reports and dashboards that improve sales visibility and accountability.
Coordinate internal resources across Development, Engineering, Marketing, Estimating and Construction to advance opportunities and ensure an exceptional customer experience.

Sales & Client Engagement

Lead prospect engagement from initial contact through contract execution.
Facilitate customer discovery meetings and identify client objectives.
Prepare and deliver sales presentations, proposals, and business development materials.
Lead RFP responses and competitive procurement opportunities.
Coordinate with Marketing to increase brand awareness and market visibility.
Support negotiation of commercial agreements and project contracts.

Project Feasibility & Development Support

Evaluate prospective opportunities for technical and commercial feasibility.
Collaborate with Engineering and Development teams during project evaluation and preconstruction efforts.
Assist with project scoping, customer communications, and incentive evaluations.
Support development activities related to utility interconnection, project economics, and incentive programs.
Coordinate smooth project handoff to Development and Operations teams.

Market Intelligence & Industry Expertise

Maintain knowledge of distributed solar, battery energy storage systems, utility regulations, incentive programs, and market trends.

Adhering to conventional elementary school methods simply because "that's how it's always been done."

Vendor & Contract Governance

Event Management

Team Leadership & Development

Manage performance, coaching, and professional development for direct reports.

15+ years of progressive IT experience, including significant experience in IT governance, compliance, risk management, business process engineering, and/or portfolio/PMO leadership.
7+ years of experience in healthcare, life sciences, pharmaceuticals, or other FDA-regulated environments.
Demonstrated experience with FDA computerized systems requirements, including 21 CFR Part 11, validation/qualification practices, Data Integrity, and Computer Software Assurance (CSA) principles.
Experience establishing or leading enterprise IT governance frameworks, policies, and standards.

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities

IT governance frameworks, operating models, and policy management.

IT portfolio management, project/product intake, and PMO practices.

Deputy Director, Digital Advertising

OVERALL POSITION DESCRIPTION

The Deputy Director, Digital Advertising and Marketing will play a vital role in our digital fundraising strategy, with an emphasis on overseeing revenue generation, advocacy lead recruitment, brand awareness building and donor acquisition through an integrated digital advertising program.

This creative, strategic, data-driven team player will be responsible for overseeing the day-to-day paid advertising efforts across paid search, paid social, display, native and other advertising venues. They will supervise and review the creation, execution and optimization of the digital fundraising strategy across those channels, including audience targeting, media planning/buying and testing. The Deputy Director will also manage the Manager of Digital Advertising and guide the strategic execution of testing plans and venturing into new platforms.

More broadly, the position will be an integral part of defining WFP USA’s growth in the digital advertising space, including actualizing monthly media spend, working with Finance to process invoices as needed, stewarding new vendor contracts, articulating paid media budgets, revenue attribution methodology, and channel strategy in a way that ensures the program prioritizes overall ROAS and new donor acquisition efficiency. This role will work within the Advertising team while being part of the broader Marketing & Communications team for World Food Program USA.

Successful candidates will demonstrate a sophisticated understanding of executing digital campaigns, engaging audiences and raising funds, and have a track record of managing direct reports. They will also demonstrate a proficiency in achieving results in a fast-paced and dynamic environment, while balancing short- and long-term organizational priorities. They are comfortable with creating revenue projections and swiftly managing budget changes on a weekly/monthly basis to achieve the highest monetary impact. They are passionate about understanding and analyzing performance data and engaging creative thinking to design compelling advertising units.

Why Join Us?

We are a dynamic, forward leaning, financially stable organization.
You will be joining an effective, committed, high-performing group of colleagues who are well-regarded in the community.
Your opinion will count, having exposure to key stakeholders in the company
You will have access to a host of inclusive benefits including parental leave, an EAP, and a wellness benefit.
You will play a crucial role in aiding the organization in their mission of ending global hunger.

Collaborative
: We are all one team
Accountable

Respectful
: We are kind to each other
Inclusive
: We champion diversity
Optimistic
: We have a make it happen attitude

We are looking for applicants who embody these values and are invested in forwarding our mission.

Oversee, review and occasionally manage the set-up design, execution, and optimization of high impact, multi-channel digital fundraising and advertising strategies, with a focus on Google Search, paid social, display, connected television (CTV), direct response television (DRTV), and other channels to raise funds, drive brand awareness, generate advocacy leads and acquire new donors to support WFP’s mission.
Partner with cross-organizational teams to run ad hoc campaigns centered around donor retention/stewardship and lead cultivation.
Manage the Manager of Digital Advertising, including conducting weekly check-ins and 2 review cycles annually as well as managing their growth plans.

Establish and maintain critical relationships with publishing networks and vendor partners, leading monthly calls and quarterly business reviews (QBRs) as needed.
Oversee advertising budgets, including the monitoring of monthly spend, weekly/monthly reporting against targets, quarterly forecasting against lead and revenue goals and actualizing monthly media spend.
Oversee reporting across channels to ensure accuracy and insights drawn are actionable month over month.
Work closely with marketing, communications and development teams to share knowledge on current and future campaigns, gather input for on-going improvements and provide strategic ideas for optimizations with a specific focus on the donor journey and upgrading one-time donors to monthly donors.
Lead liaison with external teams to ensure alignment between ad programs and other channel content. Develop cross-channel content recommendations as needed.
Stay up to date on emerging and future digital trends, new AI products as well as competitive activations across all relevant industries to identify and grow brand opportunities.
Ownership of other ad-hoc projects as assigned, including project management of certain campaigns

A well-qualified candidate will possess the following:

jobs.title: Policy Director
jobs.description:
The Environmental Protection Network (EPN) was founded in January 2017 and now has over 750 EPA alumni across the country volunteering their time to protect the integrity of EPA, human health, and the environment. We harness the expertise of former EPA career staff and confirmation-level appointees from Democratic and Republican administrations to provide the unique perspective of former regulators with decades of historical knowledge and subject matter expertise.

We are focused on building and defending the capacity of environmental agencies and the communities they serve to truly address the most urgent health and environmental crises.

We work to ensure that EPA advances policies, budgets, and institutional changes to address environmental injustices and climate, as well as other pressing public health needs.
We provide capacity-building technical assistance and training to frontline communities; non-profit organizations; and under-resourced state, local, and tribal government agencies.
We provide pro bono support to civil servants.
We educate Congress and serve as a critical resource for facts, objective analysis, and scientific rigor for reporters and other strategic partners.

Priority Deadline-

August 26th

About The Position

This role reports to the Senior Director of Policy. The Policy Director leads the strategy and execution of EPN’s national policy work, setting vision and priorities in coordination with the Senior Director of Policy. It involves managing a small team, guiding volunteer engagement in federal policy efforts both present and future, and collaborating across departments to influence rulemaking and other policymaking, enhance transparency, support litigation, safeguard science, educate Congress, and amplify EPN’s impact through communications and partnerships. The position also plays a key role in building strategic alliances with NGOs and coalitions to advance environmental policy goals primarily at the federal level.

Responsibilities Include

Program Strategy & Implementation:

Develop vision, priorities, and goals for the national policy work with input from the national policy team and in coordination with the Senior Director of Policy.
Track key metrics (comments submitted, testimony provided, amicus briefs, science advisory groups convened, products developed).
Track various proposed rulemakings and related national policy actions.
Facilitate teams of volunteers to draft comments and letters, deliver testimony, recommendations for a future EPA, support litigation, public affairs, and meet with the executive branch (including EPA, OMB, and CEQ).
Look for opportunities to share information with other NGOs and the media, educate Congress and tribal, state, and local governments.

Team Management

Directly manage 3-4 full-time senior policy associates and contractors.
Execute on all org-wide people manager responsibilities-

Execute weekly team 1×1 check-ins and weekly team shared space management.
Execute on twice-annual formal review process.
Ongoing coaching and professional development support.
Team culture activities.

Partner With The Public Affairs Team To

Partner with other NGOs and coalitions, as relevant to EPN’s work.
Coordinate collaborative efforts, including goal-driven webinars.
Educate congressional member offices and key committee staff.
Develop/influence website and digital media content.
Support and help develop press releases, tip sheets (weekly), briefs, press conferences, and related.

Manage strategic partnerships with NGOs and others on national environmental policy issues, including:

Identify opportunities to partner with like-minded organizations on relevant environmental health issues.
Represent EPN and/or find and manage volunteers to represent EPN in various coalitions operating in relevant environmental federal policy areas.

Qualifications

At least 7+ years of relevant work experience
Highly productive in remote working environments
Interest in environmental justice, US environmental and health policy, and/or the work of the EPA
Prior experience working closely with or at the EPA is preferred but not required
Experience in program management, public sector initiatives, or workforce development, preferably within environmental justice, government, or nonprofit sectors
Experience creating and operationalizing priorities, goals, and metrics
Strong cultural competency and a demonstrated commitment to racial, environmental, and social justice
Ability to manage multiple deadlines, priorities, and stakeholders in a fast-paced and evolving environment
Experience with direct people management
Experience with project management and specifically managing work across multiple complex stakeholder groups

Core Competencies

Building Relationships: In this role, building relationships means cultivating trust, credibility, and mutual respect with a wide range of stakeholders, including civil servants, volunteers, NGO partners, coalition members, and congressional staff. The ideal candidate fosters strong, values-aligned partnerships that support collaboration on national environmental policy efforts and amplify EPN’s influence. This competency also includes the ability to engage authentically across lines of difference, navigate power dynamics thoughtfully, and maintain long-term relationships that are rooted in shared goals and open communication.
Making Decisions & Demonstrating Judgement: In this role, sound decision-making and judgment are essential for navigating complex policy issues and organizational priorities. The ideal candidate assesses risks, balances stakeholder input, and makes timely, strategic choices that reflect EPN’s mission and values.
Team Management- In this role, effective team management includes coaching and developing team members while driving them toward clear, measurable outcomes. The ideal candidate provides regular feedback, supports professional growth, and creates a collaborative environment that empowers staff to lead. They ensure alignment with organizational goals and hold the team accountable to high standards of performance and impact.
Managing Execution: In this role, managing execution means ensuring that team and departmental goals are met through clear planning, consistent monitoring, and timely adjustments. The ideal candidate tracks progress against key milestones, addresses challenges proactively, and keeps work aligned with evolving priorities. They lead with focus and flexibility, ensuring high-quality outcomes in a dynamic policy landscape.
Planning: In this role, effective planning involves developing a clear vision, priorities, goals, and strategy in collaboration with key stakeholders. The ideal candidate gathers and synthesizes input, translates it into a focused and actionable plan, and ensures alignment across teams. They also create pathways for implementation, including investing in resources and support needed to bring the strategy to life.

You've already taken something from zero to scale. Now you're searching for your next significant opportunity—one with both urgency and a clear moral imperative. If you think the U.S. education system is failing gifted children and you're prepared to take action, read on.

gt.school is reimagining what education should be for high-ability students. Our 2 Hour Learning approach condenses the academic day into concentrated, mastery-oriented sessions—creating space for students to tackle meaningful challenges. We're now prepared to develop a physical prototype campus that introduces the components currently absent: leadership training, competitive peer environments, a performance-oriented culture, and the community these students have lacked.

You will oversee the creation, validation, and public launch of this prototype campus—with the objective of establishing it as the blueprint for a national system. You'll simultaneously expand our virtual GT Anywhere program alongside the existing team. This involves piloting real-world programming, generating parent interest, establishing a sustainable culture, and creating the frameworks necessary for scaling.

We require someone with the drive and authority of a founder. Someone who recognizes that strong concepts are meaningless without disciplined execution. Someone capable of transforming a clear vision into a school that parents advocate for enthusiastically—and students are eager to join.

What You Will Be Doing

Creating and piloting scalable programs that go beyond academics—emphasizing leadership development, autonomy, and competitive environments
Establishing and validating a physical prototype campus, including workforce structures, facility planning, and operational systems
Crafting parent communication strategies, market positioning, and expansion frameworks to support growth
Establishing, documenting, and replicating quality benchmarks and cultural practices across all future locations
Serving as the visible representative of the prototype—building awareness through media engagement, events, and strategic partnerships

What You Won’t Be Doing

Operating a conventional school with traditional classrooms, full teaching staff, and all-day schedules
Accommodating families seeking watered-down gifted programs featuring AP courses and limited rigor
Implementing gradual improvements within established systems—we're not "improving" schools, we're building alternatives
Prioritizing shallow engagement indicators—we focus on substantive outcomes and rigorous learning, not mere participation
Working entirely remotely—you'll have scheduling flexibility, but must spend approximately 1 week monthly in Austin to maintain operational connection

Program Director Key Responsibilities

Create, validate, and scale a high-performance educational model for gifted students—beginning with a single prototype campus and growing into a nationwide system.

Basic Requirements

Created and scaled a high-impact venture from the ground up (preferably involving physical operations or education). We are referring to at least 1M USD in annual revenue under your ownership
Substantial, direct understanding of gifted students—acquired through family experience, professional background, or personal history
AI First mentality — Preference for prioritizing AI as the primary approach to problem-solving, strategic decisions and generating work output at scale.
Demonstrated capacity to communicate a persuasive vision and turn doubters into advocates
Located in the U.S., with capacity to travel to Austin regularly (at least 1 week per month)
Authorized to work in the U.S. without requiring visa sponsorship

About GT School

GT School is revolutionizing education with AI, expert coaching, and 50+ years of learning science. They blend cutting-edge tech with data-driven insights to unlock every student's full potential.

They're on a mission to disrupt the broken education system and unleash the true potential of gifted minds. Forget the one-size-fits-all approach that leaves brilliant students bored and disengaged.

This school has tossed the rulebook and created a modern learning environment powered by AI and guided by dedicated mentors. Their personalized approach accelerates learning - 2-6 times faster than traditional classrooms.

GT School students explore their passions, develop critical thinking skills, and learn to innovate.

Because that's where genius lies.

GT School is where gifted minds turn potential into power.

There is so much to cover for this exciting role, and space here is limited. Hit the Apply button if you found this interesting and want to learn more. We look forward to meeting you!

Working with us

This is a full-time (40 hours per week), long-term position. The position is immediately available and requires entering into an independent contractor agreement with Crossover as a Contractor of Record. The compensation level for this role is $200 USD/hour, which equates to $400,000 USD/year assuming 40 hours per week and 50 weeks per year. The payment period is weekly. Consult www.crossover.com/help-and-faqs for more details on this topic.

jobs.title: Fundraising Director, Development
jobs.description:
As Director of Development you will put your proven sales and relationship management skills to work driving success and achieving revenue goals through positive engagement with staff and community volunteer leaders.

Utilizing your proven networking skills, you will identify and cultivate relationships with key community leaders and C-Suite corporate partners effectively. As a recognized leader and fundraiser in the peer-to-peer space, you will coach and inspire your team to build successful event growth strategies through community and volunteer engagement.

You join a high performing team of leaders responsible for the implementation of Walk to End Alzheimer’s®, the world’s largest fundraiser for Alzheimer’s care, support and research; Do What You Love to End ALZ, a signature event of the Alzheimer’s Association, and is one of the fastest growing and unique campaigns of its kind; and Relationship Events/Gala initiatives.

Walk to End Alzheimer’s® ranks as the second-largest peer-to-peer fundraising event in the United States and continues to set the pace as one of the fastest-growing walk events in the country. Do What You Love to End ALZ is leading the peer-to-peer fundraising space with innovation and creativity, providing an excellent opportunity to engage new audiences in the fight to end Alzheimer’s among many diverse activity groups, from the golfing and hiking communities to live streamers and bridge players.

In this key leadership role, you will be responsible for successful implementation of Walk to End Alzheimer’s®, Do What You Love to End ALZ and Gala to meet or exceed goals through staff training, coaching and mentoring as well as volunteer recruitment and empowerment, team and individual fundraising cultivation, and through the diligent execution of strategies that align with best and proven practices. You will contribute your professional fundraising leadership experience in leading, coaching and mentoring your team of professional development staff.

This position is a perfect fit for a purpose-driven, mission-minded people leader who inspires others to take initiative to achieve positive and measurable results, demonstrates a positive attitude and takes a pro-active approach to responsibility ownership.

This Role Is Right For You If

You are an enthusiastic and active member of the community, utilizing your engaging networking skills to build sustainable corporate and community partnerships to achieve organizational revenue goals
You are able to drive success and provide positive engagement with staff and volunteers through coaching, recognition, and mutual accountability
You have successfully recruited, managed, and coached fundraising staff and volunteers to effectively implement best and proven practices to achieve fundraising goals with a priority on Peer-to-Peer initiatives
You are known as a uniter and have successfully built a positive, healthy, and inclusive team environment
Your experience in providing inspirational leadership, oversight and implementation of fundraising programs has resulted in meeting or exceeding revenue goals around mass market events/special events, corporate sponsorship and other corporate gifts, pipeline development for major and planned gifts and other areas of development
You have proven success at building sustainable corporate and community relationships that contribute to achieving event revenue goals, greater community participation and heightened brand awareness
You have managed or are capable of managing multiple volunteer-led mass-market events simultaneously that have resulted in revenue growth year over year
You embrace a challenge and have achieved or surpassed designated revenue and participant goals through team and individual fundraising, corporate solicitation, and community partnerships
You have demonstrated success at prospecting, cultivating and stewarding event teams, sponsors and participants
You have excellent communication and organization skills and are comfortable with managing event budgets, training volunteers, working to set timelines and milestones and using data to affect positive outcomes

What You Bring

Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience
5-7 years of proven experience recruiting and mobilizing volunteers and community leaders to achieve goals, preferably in a peer-to-peer fundraising environment OR successful experience leading a team to meet sales targets
Demonstrated management skills, including the ability set clear goals, organize projects, establish and manage budgets, and establish accountability processes
Ability to supervise and manage Walk to End Alzheimer’s staff, including onboarding, training and development
A proven track record at building sustainable corporate and community relationships that contribute to achieving organizational and revenue goals
Proven track record of developing and implementing strategies for identifying, recruiting and engaging high-level and C-Suite volunteer leadership,
Enthusiastic willingness to work with diverse communities and build an inclusive environment
Ability and willingness to travel up to 50% within the assigned territory by car. While most such travel is same day, occasional overnight travel or air travel may be required. Must have valid driver’s license, access to reliable vehicle, good driving record and proof of automobile insurance
Ability and willingness to work evenings and weekends as required for the job
Ability to bend, stoop, lift and transport up to 25 lbs of materials
Strong computer skills, proficient with Microsoft Office products and social media; experience with, or ability to rapidly learn, Luminate/Convio software

Who We Are

The Alzheimer’s Association is the leading voluntary health organization in Alzheimer’s care, support and research. Our mission is to lead the way to end Alzheimer's and all other dementia– by accelerating global research, driving risk reduction and early detection, and maximizing quality care and support.

The Alzheimer’s Association announced a landmark $100 million investment in research for 2023. This unparalleled commitment is illustrative of the momentum we are building in dementia research — our investments today will lead to breakthroughs tomorrow.

At the Alzheimer’s Association, our employees are at the core of all we do. Our network of more than 1,750 employees across the United States makes a difference each and every day for those impacted by Alzheimer’s and those at risk for the disease.

We warmly invite qualified applicants to consider this opportunity to make a life-changing impact on the millions living with Alzheimer’s, their caregivers and those that may develop the disease in the future. Read on to learn more about the role, then visit our website www.alz.org/jobs to explore who we are and why we've been recognized as a Best Place to Work for the last twelve years in a row.

At the Alzheimer's Association®, we believe that diverse perspectives are critical to achieving health equity — meaning that all communities have a fair and just opportunity for early diagnosis and access to risk reduction and quality care. The Association is committed to engaging underrepresented and underserved communities and responding with resources and education to address the disproportionate impact of Alzheimer’s and dementia.

The Alzheimer’s Association commitment remains steadfast in engaging all communities in our full mission. The Association provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment to the fullest extent required by law, including, but not limited to, on the basis of race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, gender identity, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, or any other legally protected characteristic.

Employees working 24 hours/week or more are eligible for a comprehensive benefits package, including medical, dental, vision, flex accounts, short and long-term disability, life insurance, long term care insurance, tuition reimbursement, generous Paid Time Off, 12 annual holidays and Paid Family Leave, as well as an annual Cultural & Heritage Day and Volunteer Day of their choosing. They are also eligible for our gold standard 401(k) retirement plan. Please click HERE for more information.

Full time employees (37.5 hours/week), will enjoy all of the above plus an annual School Visitation Day and an Elder Care Facility Day of their choosing.

jobs.title: Director of Development, Alpha - $200,000/year USD
jobs.description:
Families who choose Alpha Miami surround themselves with trusted advisors across every aspect of their lives. This role fills the one gap they didn't know existed.

You will become the person they reach out to when doubt arises, when instinct tells them something isn't quite right, or when they encounter a moment they know you will grasp immediately. Your familiarity with each family will run deep enough that you anticipate needs before they surface—and you will possess both the judgment and the poise to address whatever they bring with discretion, warmth, and seamless execution. Over time, your role will extend beyond the boundaries of their child's education. You will become woven into the very way they navigate this season of family life.

Miami's independent school landscape is compact, deeply networked, and unforgiving when trust breaks. A family's perception of Alpha does not remain confined to campus—it circulates through the structures that influence opinion: the residence, the membership, the vessel, the benefit circuit, the messaging threads that determine where the next cohort enrolls. You will grasp this reality intuitively, because your career has unfolded in environments where reputation serves as the sole meaningful asset and one error endures longer than all successes combined. You will cultivate a community that families instinctively protect, where inclusion feels organic and word-of-mouth advocacy flows from earned experience.

Miami operates as an inherently global city. Your work will involve Latin American households, international corporate leaders, finance and technology families who have recently relocated to Miami, and transient families whose views on education—and institutions broadly—have been formed by experiences well beyond the American independent school framework. Many transition between Miami, São Paulo, Bogotá, Madrid, and New York with the same ease others cross neighborhoods, and they will evaluate Alpha against alternatives located anywhere globally. The ideal candidate will navigate cross-cultural family expectations—and the demand for seamless, sophisticated relationships—with the same confidence they bring to more conventional Miami private school dynamics.

Alpha does not operate as a conventional institution. Students complete foundational academics in two daily hours through AI-enabled applications, then dedicate remaining time to public speaking, critical reasoning, and applied projects. No traditional lectures. No filler assignments. Results place students in the top 1% nationally.

The families selecting Alpha have made a deliberate choice—and in a city where opinions proliferate and educational decisions signal status, they will face constant scrutiny. You will ensure they are never without a confident response. If sustaining that conviction through years of discerning, internationally-informed doubt feels taxing, this position will not suit you. If it represents the most compelling dialogue you could engage in, continue reading.

What You Will Be Doing

Shape the cultural fabric of the school community—the atmosphere, rituals, and implicit expectations that create a sense of belonging—so Alpha becomes a place families take pride in, not merely an institution they selected
Steward the entire parent journey—from initial outreach through enrollment, continued engagement, and sustained advocacy—so instructional staff remain focused on students and families consistently have a reliable point of contact
Detect early signals when dynamics shift, and address them with the care and judgment that preserve trust—including the more difficult discernment of recognizing when a family does not align with the community
Maintain visibility in the spaces families occupy: morning arrival, afternoon departure, evening gatherings, and the spontaneous exchanges that carry the most weight
Foster a community that both domestic and international families regard as precious—and where advocacy emerges organically from genuine satisfaction
Articulate Alpha's narrative persuasively—in private dialogue, at community events, and within the circles of discerning, internationally-minded families where the school's standing is truly established

What You Won’t Be Doing

Operating from behind a desk—your physical presence within the community defines the role
Adhering to conventional 9–5 schedules—early mornings, late afternoons, and evening commitments are inherent to the position, not occasional demands
Redirecting challenging parent discussions to faculty or administrative colleagues—you hold full ownership of these interactions
Relying on administrative infrastructure, established workflows, or a complete team—you function with significant independence and construct what is necessary
Approaching family relationships as transactional accounts—this role depends on authentic connection, not procedural adherence

Director Of Development Key Responsibilities

Serve as the central, trusted relationship for every family's journey at Alpha's Miami campus, and as the architect of the surrounding community culture. Maintain their confidence through challenging moments, define the traditions and tone that make belonging feel meaningful, and establish the conditions under which satisfied families transform into active advocates within the networks that influence Miami's independent school environment.

Basic Requirements

5+ years building and sustaining trust with high-net-worth or ultra-high-net-worth families in a relationship-intensive, high-touch capacity
Demonstrated success guiding discerning clients through consequential decisions—with tangible outcomes you can reference: conversion rates, retention metrics, referral volume
The discretion and composure required to navigate sensitive, confidential matters without visible impact
Proven experience managing and developing people—providing coaching, maintaining rigorous standards, and executing difficult personnel decisions—not simply managing relationships or client accounts
Innate cross-cultural fluency across both globally mobile families and established Miami households
AI-native approach—you employ AI tools with fluency, understand their strengths and limitations, and proactively introduce superior solutions, even when you are not the one building them technically
Located in Miami, available for full-time on-site presence, and adaptable to flexible scheduling
Authorized to work in the United States without requiring sponsorship

Nice-to-have Requirements

Background as a head of school, principal, superintendent, or equivalent school leadership position
Professional-level fluency in Spanish or Portuguese
Personal or professional exposure to independent or non-traditional educational models
Established connections within Miami's private school parent communities
Experience working with internationally mobile, Latin American, or globally connected households
A personal network extending through the neighborhoods, clubs, and institutions where Alpha's families reside and make decisions

About Alpha

Join the team building school around student growth

Alpha reimagines the school day around faster learning, stronger mentorship, and more time for students to build real-world skills.

Roles with real student impact:
Alpha hires teachers (guides), operators, admissions experts, school & curriculum leaders, and remote team members.

Education work that pays like it matters:
Alpha offers six-figure roles for people ready to help build a radically better school experience.

A culture built for builders:
Alpha is fast-moving, ambitious, and student focused. It’s for people who want to improve the system, not maintain it.

Alpha is where you can do the most meaningful work of your career.

There is so much to cover for this exciting role, and space here is limited. Hit the Apply button if you found this interesting and want to learn more. We look forward to meeting you!

Working with us

jobs.title: Director of Development, Alpha - $200,000/year USD
jobs.description:
Families who choose Alpha Miami surround themselves with trusted advisors across every aspect of their lives. This role fills the one gap they didn't know existed.

You will become the person they reach out to when doubt arises, when instinct tells them something isn't quite right, or when they encounter a moment they know you will grasp immediately. Your familiarity with each family will run deep enough that you anticipate needs before they surface—and you will possess both the judgment and the poise to address whatever they bring with discretion, warmth, and seamless execution. Over time, your role will extend beyond the boundaries of their child's education. You will become woven into the very way they navigate this season of family life.

Miami's independent school landscape is compact, deeply networked, and unforgiving when trust breaks. A family's perception of Alpha does not remain confined to campus—it circulates through the structures that influence opinion: the residence, the membership, the vessel, the benefit circuit, the messaging threads that determine where the next cohort enrolls. You will grasp this reality intuitively, because your career has unfolded in environments where reputation serves as the sole meaningful asset and one error endures longer than all successes combined. You will cultivate a community that families instinctively protect, where inclusion feels organic and word-of-mouth advocacy flows from earned experience.

Miami operates as an inherently global city. Your work will involve Latin American households, international corporate leaders, finance and technology families who have recently relocated to Miami, and transient families whose views on education—and institutions broadly—have been formed by experiences well beyond the American independent school framework. Many transition between Miami, São Paulo, Bogotá, Madrid, and New York with the same ease others cross neighborhoods, and they will evaluate Alpha against alternatives located anywhere globally. The ideal candidate will navigate cross-cultural family expectations—and the demand for seamless, sophisticated relationships—with the same confidence they bring to more conventional Miami private school dynamics.

Alpha does not operate as a conventional institution. Students complete foundational academics in two daily hours through AI-enabled applications, then dedicate remaining time to public speaking, critical reasoning, and applied projects. No traditional lectures. No filler assignments. Results place students in the top 1% nationally.

The families selecting Alpha have made a deliberate choice—and in a city where opinions proliferate and educational decisions signal status, they will face constant scrutiny. You will ensure they are never without a confident response. If sustaining that conviction through years of discerning, internationally-informed doubt feels taxing, this position will not suit you. If it represents the most compelling dialogue you could engage in, continue reading.

Shape the cultural fabric of the school community—the atmosphere, rituals, and implicit expectations that create a sense of belonging—so Alpha becomes a place families take pride in, not merely an institution they selected
Steward the entire parent journey—from initial outreach through enrollment, continued engagement, and sustained advocacy—so instructional staff remain focused on students and families consistently have a reliable point of contact
Detect early signals when dynamics shift, and address them with the care and judgment that preserve trust—including the more difficult discernment of recognizing when a family does not align with the community
Maintain visibility in the spaces families occupy: morning arrival, afternoon departure, evening gatherings, and the spontaneous exchanges that carry the most weight
Foster a community that both domestic and international families regard as precious—and where advocacy emerges organically from genuine satisfaction
Articulate Alpha's narrative persuasively—in private dialogue, at community events, and within the circles of discerning, internationally-minded families where the school's standing is truly established

What You Won’t Be Doing

Operating from behind a desk—your physical presence within the community defines the role
Adhering to conventional 9–5 schedules—early mornings, late afternoons, and evening commitments are inherent to the position, not occasional demands
Redirecting challenging parent discussions to faculty or administrative colleagues—you hold full ownership of these interactions
Relying on administrative infrastructure, established workflows, or a complete team—you function with significant independence and construct what is necessary
Approaching family relationships as transactional accounts—this role depends on authentic connection, not procedural adherence

Director Of Development Key Responsibilities

Serve as the central, trusted relationship for every family's journey at Alpha's Miami campus, and as the architect of the surrounding community culture. Maintain their confidence through challenging moments, define the traditions and tone that make belonging feel meaningful, and establish the conditions under which satisfied families transform into active advocates within the networks that influence Miami's independent school environment.

Basic Requirements

5+ years building and sustaining trust with high-net-worth or ultra-high-net-worth families in a relationship-intensive, high-touch capacity
Demonstrated success guiding discerning clients through consequential decisions—with tangible outcomes you can reference: conversion rates, retention metrics, referral volume
The discretion and composure required to navigate sensitive, confidential matters without visible impact
Proven experience managing and developing people—providing coaching, maintaining rigorous standards, and executing difficult personnel decisions—not simply managing relationships or client accounts
Innate cross-cultural fluency across both globally mobile families and established Miami households
AI-native approach—you employ AI tools with fluency, understand their strengths and limitations, and proactively introduce superior solutions, even when you are not the one building them technically
Located in Miami, available for full-time on-site presence, and adaptable to flexible scheduling
Authorized to work in the United States without requiring sponsorship

Nice-to-have Requirements

Background as a head of school, principal, superintendent, or equivalent school leadership position
Professional-level fluency in Spanish or Portuguese
Personal or professional exposure to independent or non-traditional educational models
Established connections within Miami's private school parent communities
Experience working with internationally mobile, Latin American, or globally connected households
A personal network extending through the neighborhoods, clubs, and institutions where Alpha's families reside and make decisions

jobs.title: Director of Advancement, Alpha - $400,000/year USD
jobs.description:
Families who enroll at Alpha don't typically find us through advertising. They come because someone they trust—at a dinner table, in a living room—told them, "This transformed my child." Your job is to own and expand that word-of-mouth ecosystem across an entire region: the gatherings, the parent advocates, the relationship with the mayor's office, the executive who provides a 14-year-old with their first meaningful project.

In a typical week, you'll be present in four different rooms. You design and execute the region's event calendar, hosting everything from a 150-person open house to an intimate eight-person dinner, running several each month. You identify and train current parents who are genuinely eager to speak with prospective families, and you facilitate those one-to-one connections. You cultivate relationships with civic leaders and business executives, converting those ties into event venues, support for new campus launches, and tangible opportunities for students. And you deliver the Alpha Networks promise: facilitating introductions, expert-led masterclasses, internships, alumni transitions—all tracked family by family.

There is no complete manual to follow. You build the playbook as you execute it, and the processes you develop become models for colleagues doing the same work in other cities. As your region scales, the performance bar rises: doors opened per enrolled family must increase even as total enrollment grows. Your success is measured by the proportion of growth driven by authentic personal endorsements, evaluated over years rather than quarters.

No degree or institutional pedigree is required. An MBA, a background in consulting or wealth management, or a self-built career in community organizing, hospitality, or advancement are all valued equally. What matters is your demonstrated ability to bring people together and convert those relationships into measurable outcomes.

This is an on-site position based in one of the following regions: San Francisco, Los Angeles, San Diego, Denver, Greenwich, Miami, Atlanta, Boston, Oklahoma City, Tulsa, Dorado, Nashville, or Park City. The role requires evening and weekend availability in settings with high-expectation parents, elected officials, and business founders, as well as frequent local travel. You will become the most well-connected person in your city, and you will leverage that network for the benefit of students. If that exchange sounds like the purpose rather than the sacrifice, we encourage you to apply.

What You Will Be Doing

Creating and executing the region's event calendar: open-format gatherings, curated dinners organized by city and grade level, and family retreats, managing several per month within budget
Identifying and securing venues, hosts, and vendors, and personally hosting each event
Identifying and training current parents to serve as ambassadors, providing them with authentic narratives, and facilitating introductions to prospective families and campus tours
Establishing relationships with public officials and business leaders, and converting those connections into event venues, support for campus expansion, and opportunities for students
Facilitating connections between enrolled families in parent circles and placing students in mentorships, masterclasses, and real-world internships; welcoming graduating families into the alumni network within 30 days
Recording every event, introduction, and first-contact source in the CRM (customer relationship management platform) to ensure "doors opened per family" is an accurate, trackable metric

What You Won’t Be Doing

Purchasing growth through paid media, ad spend, or impression-based lead generation
Creating the brand narrative or executing top-down marketing campaigns; that responsibility belongs to Marketing
Managing admissions logistics, conducting tours, or handling enrollment documentation; Admissions and Family Success own those functions
Operating a campus on a daily basis or managing facility access
Treating raw attendance and headcount as success metrics
Waiting for a finalized playbook, standard templates, or dedicated support staff before beginning

Director Of Advancement Key Responsibilities

Drive people-first referrals as the primary source of enrollment growth in your region.

Basic Requirements

5+ years building community or relationship-driven programs in K-12 education, membership organizations, or similar network businesses, where growth was driven by referrals, members, congregations, chapters, alumni, or client relationships, with quantifiable results
Personal experience designing and executing 20+ events across formats, from intimate curated dinners to gatherings of 100+ attendees, with full budget accountability
Established and sustained relationships with public officials or business executives that resulted in specific, documentable outcomes
Consistent CRM discipline; tracking relationships, attributions, and actions is an established practice
Currently resides in, or willing to relocate to, one of these regions: San Francisco, Los Angeles, San Diego, Denver, Greenwich (CT), Miami, Atlanta, Boston, Oklahoma City, Tulsa, Dorado (PR), Nashville, or Park City (UT)
Authorized to work in the US without visa sponsorship

Nice-to-have Requirements

Led regional growth, community engagement, or partnership initiatives for a network-oriented organization: a school network, membership association, franchise system, or faith-based or civic institution
Developed and monetized a high-trust relationship portfolio as a client-facing leader in wealth management, consulting, or business development
Advanced through roles in admissions, advancement, community organizing, or hospitality, and consistently served as the institution's public representative and host
Established connections with local government or the business community in your region
Deep understanding of how families navigate high-stakes educational decisions

jobs.description:
Families who select Alpha Miami have relied on trusted advisors across every facet of their lives. This is the one relationship they haven't yet had.

You will become the person they reach out to when something doesn't feel quite right, when uncertainty surfaces, or when they want to share a moment with someone who truly understands. You will develop a deep familiarity with each family—anticipating their needs before they articulate them—and you will possess the judgment and composure to respond to whatever they bring you with warmth, discretion, and complete ease. Over time, you won't simply represent the school their child attends. You will become woven into the way they experience this meaningful stage of family life.

The private school landscape in Miami is tightly knit, interconnected, and intolerant of errors. A family's journey at Alpha does not remain confined to the school itself—it reverberates through influential networks: residential buildings, private clubs, yachts, philanthropic events, and the WhatsApp channels that quietly determine where the next cohort enrolls. You will intuitively grasp this reality, because your career has unfolded in environments where reputation is the singular form of capital and one mistake can eclipse years of success. You will cultivate a community that families regard with a sense of ownership, where inclusion feels natural and word-of-mouth referrals emerge because the experience genuinely deserves them.

Miami operates as a global hub by nature. You will engage with families from Latin America, multinational executives, finance and technology professionals who have recently relocated to Miami, and globally mobile households whose perspectives on education—and institutions more broadly—are informed by experiences well beyond the typical American independent school framework. Many navigate between Miami, São Paulo, Bogotá, Madrid, and New York with the same fluidity others exhibit crossing neighborhoods, and they will evaluate Alpha against educational options worldwide. The ideal candidate for this role will be equally adept at navigating cross-cultural family contexts—and the expectation of seamless, sophisticated relationships—as they are the more recognizable dynamics of Miami's private school environment.

Alpha does not follow conventional school models. Students complete their core academic work in two hours per day using AI-powered applications, then dedicate the remainder of their time to public speaking, critical thinking, and applied projects. No traditional lectures. No unnecessary assignments. Performance outcomes in the top 1% nationally.

The families who select Alpha have made a deliberate choice—and in a city where opinions are abundant and educational decisions carry social weight, they will be expected to justify that choice repeatedly. You will ensure they are never caught without a confident answer. If sustaining that conviction through years of refined, globally informed skepticism feels daunting, this position is not suited to you. If it represents the most compelling professional conversation you could engage in, continue reading.

What You Will Be Doing

Shape the cultural identity of the school community—the atmosphere, rituals, and implicit standards that foster a sense of belonging—so that Alpha becomes a source of pride for families, not merely an institution they selected
Steward the parent relationship from beginning to end—from initial inquiry through enrollment, ongoing engagement, and sustained advocacy—so teaching staff remain focused on students and families consistently have a reliable point of contact
Detect early when something is amiss, and address it with the discretion and judgment that preserves trust—including the more difficult discernment of recognizing when a family is not the right match
Maintain visibility where families are: morning arrival, afternoon departure, evening gatherings, and the informal exchanges that carry the greatest weight
Foster a community that both domestic and international families regard protectively—and where advocacy arises organically because the experience merits it
Convey Alpha's narrative persuasively—in individual dialogues, at community events, and within the circles of discerning, internationally connected families where the school's standing is truly established

What You Won’t Be Doing

Operating from behind a desk—your visible presence within the community defines the role
Adhering to standard 9–5 schedules—early morning availability, late afternoon engagement, and evening events are integral to the position, not occasional occurrences
Redirecting challenging parent discussions to faculty or administrators—you assume full ownership of these conversations
Relying on administrative infrastructure, established systems, or a complete team—you function with substantial autonomy and create what is necessary
Approaching family relationships as transactional accounts—this role rewards authentic connection, not procedural adherence

Director Of Advancement Key Responsibilities

Serve as the central trusted relationship for every family's experience at Alpha's Miami campus, and act as the curator of the community's cultural identity. Maintain their confidence during challenging moments, establish the traditions and tone that make belonging feel meaningful, and cultivate the conditions under which satisfied families become articulate advocates within the networks that influence Miami's independent school landscape.

Basic Requirements

5+ years building and sustaining trust with high-net-worth or ultra-high-net-worth families in a high-touch, relationship-centered capacity
A demonstrated history of guiding sophisticated clients through consequential decisions—with measurable results you can articulate: conversion rates, retention figures, referral growth
The discretion and poise to navigate sensitive, confidential matters without compromising relationships
A proven record of managing and developing people—providing coaching, upholding rigorous standards, and making difficult personnel judgments—not simply managing relationships or client portfolios
Intuitive cross-cultural fluency with both globally mobile and long-established Miami families
AI-first orientation—you leverage AI tools with ease, understand their strengths and limitations, and proactively identify superior alternatives, even if you are not developing them yourself
Residing in Miami, available full-time on-site, and comfortable with non-standard hours
Authorized to work in the United States without requiring sponsorship

Nice-to-have Requirements

Background as a head of school, principal, superintendent, or in a similar school leadership capacity
Professional proficiency in Spanish or Portuguese
Personal or professional exposure to independent or non-traditional educational models
Established connections within Miami's private school parent communities
Experience working with internationally mobile, Latin American, or globally connected families
A personal network that extends through the neighborhoods, clubs, and institutions where Alpha's families reside and make decisions

Tencent Games was established in 2003. We are a leading global platform for game development, operations and publishing, and the largest online game community in China. Meanwhile, we actively promote the development of esports industry, work with global partners to build an open, collaborative and symbiotic industrial ecology, and create high-quality digital life experiences for players.

Director of Strategic Partnerships - North America

About The Role

Tencent Games is looking for a senior partnerships leader to own and deepen our relationships with the most important companies in Western gaming — first-party platforms, major publishers, and leading developers. This is a relationship-first role for someone who can open doors at the executive level, turn conversations into long-term strategic partnerships, and represent Tencent credibly with the industry's most senior decision-makers.

What You'll Do

Own senior-level relationships with key platform and publisher partners, serving as a trusted point of contact from working teams up to the C-suite
Identify, shape, and drive strategic partnership opportunities end-to-end — from first conversation through structuring, alignment, and execution
Partner closely with business unit leadership and cross-functional teams (studios, publishing, investment, legal) to land and deliver on partnership commitments
Bring sharp, timely market and competitive intelligence back into the organization to inform strategy and deal priorities
Represent Tencent Games at major industry events, conferences, and executive forums

Who We Look For

Based in North America with 10+ years in gaming, or in consulting/banking with deep gaming sector exposure
An existing network across platforms and publishers — established C-suite and senior executive relationships are a strong plus
A natural relationship builder who thrives on opening new doors: comfortable cold-calling a studio founder on Monday and presenting to a platform executive on Friday
Equally strong as a team player and an independent operator — you don't wait to be handed opportunities
Outstanding communication, analytical, and interpersonal skills; comfortable with ambiguity and matrixed organizations
Genuine passion for games and the business behind them

US-California-Los Angeles, US-California-Palo Alto, US-New York State-New York, US-Washington-Bellevue
