new_jobs.title: Director of Advancement, Alpha - $400,000/year USD
new_jobs.description:
Families who enroll at Alpha don't typically find us through advertising. They come because someone they trust—at a dinner table, in a living room—told them, "This transformed my child." Your job is to own and expand that word-of-mouth ecosystem across an entire region: the gatherings, the parent advocates, the relationship with the mayor's office, the executive who provides a 14-year-old with their first meaningful project.

In a typical week, you'll be present in four different rooms. You design and execute the region's event calendar, hosting everything from a 150-person open house to an intimate eight-person dinner, running several each month. You identify and train current parents who are genuinely eager to speak with prospective families, and you facilitate those one-to-one connections. You cultivate relationships with civic leaders and business executives, converting those ties into event venues, support for new campus launches, and tangible opportunities for students. And you deliver the Alpha Networks promise: facilitating introductions, expert-led masterclasses, internships, alumni transitions—all tracked family by family.

There is no complete manual to follow. You build the playbook as you execute it, and the processes you develop become models for colleagues doing the same work in other cities. As your region scales, the performance bar rises: doors opened per enrolled family must increase even as total enrollment grows. Your success is measured by the proportion of growth driven by authentic personal endorsements, evaluated over years rather than quarters.

No degree or institutional pedigree is required. An MBA, a background in consulting or wealth management, or a self-built career in community organizing, hospitality, or advancement are all valued equally. What matters is your demonstrated ability to bring people together and convert those relationships into measurable outcomes.

This is an on-site position based in one of the following regions: San Francisco, Los Angeles, San Diego, Denver, Greenwich, Miami, Atlanta, Boston, Oklahoma City, Tulsa, Dorado, Nashville, or Park City. The role requires evening and weekend availability in settings with high-expectation parents, elected officials, and business founders, as well as frequent local travel. You will become the most well-connected person in your city, and you will leverage that network for the benefit of students. If that exchange sounds like the purpose rather than the sacrifice, we encourage you to apply.

What You Will Be Doing

Creating and executing the region's event calendar: open-format gatherings, curated dinners organized by city and grade level, and family retreats, managing several per month within budget
Identifying and securing venues, hosts, and vendors, and personally hosting each event
Identifying and training current parents to serve as ambassadors, providing them with authentic narratives, and facilitating introductions to prospective families and campus tours
Establishing relationships with public officials and business leaders, and converting those connections into event venues, support for campus expansion, and opportunities for students
Facilitating connections between enrolled families in parent circles and placing students in mentorships, masterclasses, and real-world internships; welcoming graduating families into the alumni network within 30 days
Recording every event, introduction, and first-contact source in the CRM (customer relationship management platform) to ensure "doors opened per family" is an accurate, trackable metric

What You Won’t Be Doing

Purchasing growth through paid media, ad spend, or impression-based lead generation
Creating the brand narrative or executing top-down marketing campaigns; that responsibility belongs to Marketing
Managing admissions logistics, conducting tours, or handling enrollment documentation; Admissions and Family Success own those functions
Operating a campus on a daily basis or managing facility access
Treating raw attendance and headcount as success metrics
Waiting for a finalized playbook, standard templates, or dedicated support staff before beginning

Director Of Advancement Key Responsibilities

Drive people-first referrals as the primary source of enrollment growth in your region.

Basic Requirements

5+ years building community or relationship-driven programs in K-12 education, membership organizations, or similar network businesses, where growth was driven by referrals, members, congregations, chapters, alumni, or client relationships, with quantifiable results
Personal experience designing and executing 20+ events across formats, from intimate curated dinners to gatherings of 100+ attendees, with full budget accountability
Established and sustained relationships with public officials or business executives that resulted in specific, documentable outcomes
Consistent CRM discipline; tracking relationships, attributions, and actions is an established practice
Currently resides in, or willing to relocate to, one of these regions: San Francisco, Los Angeles, San Diego, Denver, Greenwich (CT), Miami, Atlanta, Boston, Oklahoma City, Tulsa, Dorado (PR), Nashville, or Park City (UT)
Authorized to work in the US without visa sponsorship

Nice-to-have Requirements

Led regional growth, community engagement, or partnership initiatives for a network-oriented organization: a school network, membership association, franchise system, or faith-based or civic institution
Developed and monetized a high-trust relationship portfolio as a client-facing leader in wealth management, consulting, or business development
Advanced through roles in admissions, advancement, community organizing, or hospitality, and consistently served as the institution's public representative and host
Established connections with local government or the business community in your region
Deep understanding of how families navigate high-stakes educational decisions

new_jobs.description:
Families who select Alpha Miami have relied on trusted advisors across every facet of their lives. This is the one relationship they haven't yet had.

You will become the person they reach out to when something doesn't feel quite right, when uncertainty surfaces, or when they want to share a moment with someone who truly understands. You will develop a deep familiarity with each family—anticipating their needs before they articulate them—and you will possess the judgment and composure to respond to whatever they bring you with warmth, discretion, and complete ease. Over time, you won't simply represent the school their child attends. You will become woven into the way they experience this meaningful stage of family life.

The private school landscape in Miami is tightly knit, interconnected, and intolerant of errors. A family's journey at Alpha does not remain confined to the school itself—it reverberates through influential networks: residential buildings, private clubs, yachts, philanthropic events, and the WhatsApp channels that quietly determine where the next cohort enrolls. You will intuitively grasp this reality, because your career has unfolded in environments where reputation is the singular form of capital and one mistake can eclipse years of success. You will cultivate a community that families regard with a sense of ownership, where inclusion feels natural and word-of-mouth referrals emerge because the experience genuinely deserves them.

Miami operates as a global hub by nature. You will engage with families from Latin America, multinational executives, finance and technology professionals who have recently relocated to Miami, and globally mobile households whose perspectives on education—and institutions more broadly—are informed by experiences well beyond the typical American independent school framework. Many navigate between Miami, São Paulo, Bogotá, Madrid, and New York with the same fluidity others exhibit crossing neighborhoods, and they will evaluate Alpha against educational options worldwide. The ideal candidate for this role will be equally adept at navigating cross-cultural family contexts—and the expectation of seamless, sophisticated relationships—as they are the more recognizable dynamics of Miami's private school environment.

Alpha does not follow conventional school models. Students complete their core academic work in two hours per day using AI-powered applications, then dedicate the remainder of their time to public speaking, critical thinking, and applied projects. No traditional lectures. No unnecessary assignments. Performance outcomes in the top 1% nationally.

The families who select Alpha have made a deliberate choice—and in a city where opinions are abundant and educational decisions carry social weight, they will be expected to justify that choice repeatedly. You will ensure they are never caught without a confident answer. If sustaining that conviction through years of refined, globally informed skepticism feels daunting, this position is not suited to you. If it represents the most compelling professional conversation you could engage in, continue reading.

What You Will Be Doing

Shape the cultural identity of the school community—the atmosphere, rituals, and implicit standards that foster a sense of belonging—so that Alpha becomes a source of pride for families, not merely an institution they selected
Steward the parent relationship from beginning to end—from initial inquiry through enrollment, ongoing engagement, and sustained advocacy—so teaching staff remain focused on students and families consistently have a reliable point of contact
Detect early when something is amiss, and address it with the discretion and judgment that preserves trust—including the more difficult discernment of recognizing when a family is not the right match
Maintain visibility where families are: morning arrival, afternoon departure, evening gatherings, and the informal exchanges that carry the greatest weight
Foster a community that both domestic and international families regard protectively—and where advocacy arises organically because the experience merits it
Convey Alpha's narrative persuasively—in individual dialogues, at community events, and within the circles of discerning, internationally connected families where the school's standing is truly established

What You Won’t Be Doing

Operating from behind a desk—your visible presence within the community defines the role
Adhering to standard 9–5 schedules—early morning availability, late afternoon engagement, and evening events are integral to the position, not occasional occurrences
Redirecting challenging parent discussions to faculty or administrators—you assume full ownership of these conversations
Relying on administrative infrastructure, established systems, or a complete team—you function with substantial autonomy and create what is necessary
Approaching family relationships as transactional accounts—this role rewards authentic connection, not procedural adherence

Director Of Advancement Key Responsibilities

Serve as the central trusted relationship for every family's experience at Alpha's Miami campus, and act as the curator of the community's cultural identity. Maintain their confidence during challenging moments, establish the traditions and tone that make belonging feel meaningful, and cultivate the conditions under which satisfied families become articulate advocates within the networks that influence Miami's independent school landscape.

Basic Requirements

5+ years building and sustaining trust with high-net-worth or ultra-high-net-worth families in a high-touch, relationship-centered capacity
A demonstrated history of guiding sophisticated clients through consequential decisions—with measurable results you can articulate: conversion rates, retention figures, referral growth
The discretion and poise to navigate sensitive, confidential matters without compromising relationships
A proven record of managing and developing people—providing coaching, upholding rigorous standards, and making difficult personnel judgments—not simply managing relationships or client portfolios
Intuitive cross-cultural fluency with both globally mobile and long-established Miami families
AI-first orientation—you leverage AI tools with ease, understand their strengths and limitations, and proactively identify superior alternatives, even if you are not developing them yourself
Residing in Miami, available full-time on-site, and comfortable with non-standard hours
Authorized to work in the United States without requiring sponsorship

Nice-to-have Requirements

Background as a head of school, principal, superintendent, or in a similar school leadership capacity
Professional proficiency in Spanish or Portuguese
Personal or professional exposure to independent or non-traditional educational models
Established connections within Miami's private school parent communities
Experience working with internationally mobile, Latin American, or globally connected families
A personal network that extends through the neighborhoods, clubs, and institutions where Alpha's families reside and make decisions

Tencent Games was established in 2003. We are a leading global platform for game development, operations and publishing, and the largest online game community in China. Meanwhile, we actively promote the development of esports industry, work with global partners to build an open, collaborative and symbiotic industrial ecology, and create high-quality digital life experiences for players.

Director of Strategic Partnerships - North America

About The Role

Tencent Games is looking for a senior partnerships leader to own and deepen our relationships with the most important companies in Western gaming — first-party platforms, major publishers, and leading developers. This is a relationship-first role for someone who can open doors at the executive level, turn conversations into long-term strategic partnerships, and represent Tencent credibly with the industry's most senior decision-makers.

What You'll Do

Own senior-level relationships with key platform and publisher partners, serving as a trusted point of contact from working teams up to the C-suite
Identify, shape, and drive strategic partnership opportunities end-to-end — from first conversation through structuring, alignment, and execution
Partner closely with business unit leadership and cross-functional teams (studios, publishing, investment, legal) to land and deliver on partnership commitments
Bring sharp, timely market and competitive intelligence back into the organization to inform strategy and deal priorities
Represent Tencent Games at major industry events, conferences, and executive forums

Who We Look For

Based in North America with 10+ years in gaming, or in consulting/banking with deep gaming sector exposure
An existing network across platforms and publishers — established C-suite and senior executive relationships are a strong plus
A natural relationship builder who thrives on opening new doors: comfortable cold-calling a studio founder on Monday and presenting to a platform executive on Friday
Equally strong as a team player and an independent operator — you don't wait to be handed opportunities
Outstanding communication, analytical, and interpersonal skills; comfortable with ambiguity and matrixed organizations
Genuine passion for games and the business behind them

Location State(s)

A DAY IN THE LIFE

Provides executive leadership for the integration, coordination, and governance of a large-scale, multi-contract integrated energy campus. Responsible for aligning scope, schedule, cost, and risk across all EPC contracts, business units, and stakeholders within the campus to ensure successful delivery.

Engages during early-stage development and project structuring to support alignment of engineering, commercial strategy, and execution approach—helping identify and mitigate integration risks before execution begins.

Serves as the central integration leader across generation, transmission, storage, gas, and data center infrastructure—ensuring alignment between independently executed scopes while enabling Business Units to deliver their work effectively.

Leads delivery of both in-front of the meter (FTM) and behind-the-meter (BTM) integrated energy campuses serving hyperscale data center clients requiring Five-Nines (99.999%) system reliability and Day 1 firm power with no ramp-up tolerance. Directs integration of solar, wind, BESS, natural gas generation, and high-voltage infrastructure into a single campus system, ensuring controls, SCADA, protection systems, and commissioning sequencing are aligned across all scopes before energization.

STEP INTO THE ROLE

Leads campus-level coordination across all scopes and contracts within the assigned integrated energy campus.
Owns the integrated campus schedule across all EPC scopes and contracts.
Serves as a senior integration leader and primary client interface at the campus level.
Supports alignment of commercial strategies across all campus contracts, including contract structures, risk allocation, and delivery models.
Engages in early-stage development to support alignment of engineering, permitting, and execution strategies.
Provides campus-level visibility into cost, schedule, and financial performance across all contracts and scopes.
Establishes and manages campus-level risk strategies, with emphasis on cross-contract and interface risks.
Leads and influences cross-functional teams across all Business Units and scopes within the campus.
Represents the organization in industry forums, client engagements, and strategic partnerships.

What You’ll Need

Bachelor’s degree in engineering, construction management, or related field; or equivalent combinations of technical training and/or related experience.
12+ years of experience in energy infrastructure, power generation, or large-scale construction programs.
7+ years in leadership roles; complex industrial projects, multi-technology project experience required.

What Sets You Apart

BTM/behind-the-meter campus delivery experience will be considered an advantage.

How We Invest In You

Competitive pay
100% employer paid HDHP insurance premiums for employees
401(k) with company match
HSA and FSA options
Dental and Vision insurance
Education Assistance (Tuition Reimbursement)
Work/Life balance
Employee/Family focused culture
Gym on site
And more!

new_jobs.description:
Why USAA?

At USAA, our mission is to empower our members to achieve financial security through highly competitive products, exceptional service and trusted advice. We seek to be the #1 choice for the military community and their families.

Embrace a fulfilling career at USAA, where our core values – honesty, integrity, loyalty and service – define how we treat each other and our members. Be part of what truly makes us special and impactful.

We are proud to support active-duty military spouses. USAA roles may offer remote or hybrid flexibility for active-duty military spouses consistent with applicable policy and business needs.

The Opportunity

As an Executive Director, Attorney, you will lead a team of attorneys and legal support professionals responsible for delivering strategic legal advice, counsel, and services to business partners across the organization. In this role, you will ensure the highest level of client service while providing guidance on products, services, operations, and business processes to support organizational objectives and maintain compliance with applicable legal and regulatory requirements.

You will oversee the identification, assessment, monitoring, and mitigation of legal risks, while implementing processes and best practices that enhance team productivity, operational efficiency, and regulatory compliance. Additionally, you will drive effective resource management and foster the professional growth and development of attorneys and support staff, ensuring a high-performing and collaborative legal team.

We offer a flexible work environment that requires an individual to be in the office 4 days per week.
This position can be based in one of the following locations: San Antonio, TX, Plano, TX, Phoenix, AZ, Colorado Springs, CO, Charlotte, NC, or Tampa, FL (Chesapeake, VA – Property and Casualty roles ONLY). Relocation assistance is available for this position.

What You'll Do

Provides counsel to enable the client to implement strategic initiatives, influencing decisions and managing risks to achieve strategic goals.
Collaborates with clients and other enterprise stakeholders and leads the execution of legal strategy, considering USAA's business strategy and regulatory requirements.
Proactively identifies strategic and tactical opportunities to improve operational effectiveness and optimal productivity, including developing and implementing best practices, ensuring quality of the work performed by members of the team and by supporting change efforts.
Ensures timely, accurate and cost-effective legal advice is provided to senior management regarding legal and regulatory matters.
Leads broad, enterprise and functional area projects.
Leads, builds and oversees a high performing team of lawyers and legal professionals through ongoing execution of recruiting, development, retention, coaching and support, performance management, and managerial activities.
Ensures risks associated with business activities are effectively identified, measured, monitored, and controlled in accordance with risk and compliance policies and procedures.

What You Have

Bachelor's degree; OR 4 years of relevant education and/or experience.
Licensed and in good standing to practice law in one state or a territory of the USA.
8 years of experience practicing law.
10 years of progressive related experience developing legal strategies, managing major initiatives and delivering results within a complex matrix environment.
4 years of direct team lead or management experience.
Experience collaborating with key resources and stakeholders, providing legal counsel to effectively influence decisions and managing legal advice and guidance efforts to achieve strategic goals.
Executive-level business acumen in the areas of business operations, industry practices and emerging trends for in-house legal counsel.

What Sets You Apart

Deep in-house legal experience supporting Property & Casualty and/or Life Insurance businesses, coupled with a demonstrated ability to serve as a trusted thought partner to executive leadership on business strategy, growth, and transformation.
Proven ability to identify emerging legal, regulatory, and market trends and translate them into actionable guidance for the business, particularly in areas such as AI adoption, product modernization, evolving distribution models, and innovation.
Strategic and creative problem-solving skills, with a track record of helping business leaders navigate ambiguity, unlock opportunities, and achieve objectives through practical, risk-informed solutions.
Experience influencing enterprise-wide initiatives that span multiple business lines and stakeholders, bringing together legal, operational, and strategic considerations to drive successful outcomes.
A forward-looking leadership approach with demonstrated success building and developing high-performing legal teams while fostering a culture of collaboration, innovation, and business partnership.
US military experience through military service or a military spouse/domestic partner.

Compensation range:

new_jobs.description:
At Veracyte, we offer exciting career opportunities for those interested in joining a pioneering team that is committed to transforming cancer care for patients across the globe. Working at Veracyte enables our employees to not only make a meaningful impact on the lives of patients, but to also learn and grow within a purpose driven environment. This is what we call the Veracyte way – it’s about how we work together, guided by our values, to give clinicians the insights they need to help patients make life-changing decisions.

Our Values

We Seek A Better Way: We pursue bold ideas, embrace complexity, and keep pushing forward.
We Make It Happen: We act with urgency, deliver with excellence, and always find a way.
We Are Stronger Together: We engage with empathy, align around what's best for Veracyte, and celebrate as one team.
We Care Deeply: We show up with integrity, kindness, and respect for one another.

The Position

Veracyte is seeking an Executive Director, Enterprise Program Management Office (PMO) to play a central role in helping us fulfill our mission to transform cancer care with breakthrough molecular diagnostics and AI insights for patients and providers worldwide, leveraging our whole transcriptome and whole genome multi-omics platform. Reporting directly to the Chief Development and Technology Officer, this leader will help accelerate Veracyte’s growth, technical capabilities, and expanding product offerings in key cancer indications by strengthening how we advance strategic initiatives from concept through feasibility, development, and launch. This is a highly visible, high-impact role for a collaborative and trusted leader who can build a next-generation Product Development Process (PDP) that brings rigor, speed, accountability, and clear decision-making to our most important work while reflecting Veracyte’s values of innovation, collaboration, and making it happen.

This position is a hybrid role based out of our San Diego office.

What You’ll Do

Transform Veracyte’s Product Development Process (PDP) into a scalable operating model for advancing initiatives from concept through launch.
Lead enterprise portfolio governance, including intake, prioritization, stage gates, sequencing, escalations, and executive trade-off decisions.
Facilitate monthly executive updates that create shared visibility, thoughtful decisions, and timely resolution of risks, dependencies, and blockers.
Lead quarterly capacity planning to align priorities, resources, timelines, and trade-offs.
Own annual program intake process and portfolio alignment accounting for budget, capacity, business value, and strategic fit.
Standardize program cadence, templates, dashboards, decision records, timelines, risk tracking, and action management.
Strengthen timeline reliability, milestone integrity, critical-path focus, and launch excellence
Define portfolio KPIs for velocity, operational readiness, resource use, and value realization
Serve as a trusted partner across Product, R&D, Operations, Bioinformatics, Software, Finance, Quality, Regulatory, Legal, Commercial, and Market Access.
Prepare clear executive and Board communications, including decision briefs, portfolio updates, risk summaries, and program investment landscape.
Build and lead a high-performing PMO team including hiring, career development, best practices, and a clear vision for the function.

Who You Are

Executive-level PMO, product portfolio management (PPM), or product governance leadership in complex, regulated environments.
Deep expertise in product development, stage-gate governance, portfolio prioritization, resource planning, risk management, and launch readiness.
Proven ability to transform fragmented practices into standardized, scalable, data-driven execution systems.
Strong business acumen, with the ability to connect investment, resources, capacity, trade-offs, and ROI.
Exceptional executive communication skills for senior leadership and development teams alike
Independent judgment and influence to surface risks, resolve blockers, clarify decisions, and help teams move forward.
Strategic thinker who can design operating models while diving into details and solving problems when execution requires it.
Passion for building a PMO center of excellence through coaching, upskilling, practical standards, and shared best practices.
Urgency balanced with quality, collaboration, and patient impact, using agile product development methods to improve speed and transparency.
A personable leadership style grounded in clarity, coaching, accountability, humility, and trust.

Preferred Qualifications

13+ years in program management, portfolio management, product development, or related leadership roles, including 8+ years leading teams or enterprise programs.
Bachelor’s degree in life sciences, engineering, business, or related field required; advanced degree, MBA, or program/portfolio certification preferred.
Experience in diagnostics, life sciences, medtech, biotech, pharmaceutical, or other regulated product environments.
Balancing clinical, regulatory, quality, laboratory, tech, and commercial launch dependencies.
Experience integrating PDP, quality management system (QMS), software development lifecycle (SDLC), and portfolio-management tools.
Ability to build governance mechanisms, dashboards, and cadences that improve transparency and decision quality.
Experience with portfolio analytics, scenario planning, capacity modeling, and value-based prioritization.
Experience implementing enterprise project tools, dashboards, and reporting systems as a reliable source of truth.
Change-management experience rolling out new ways of working.
Aptitude with modern AI tools to automate routine work, improve reporting, and increase PMO productivity.

For candidates based in our San Diego office
, the salary range is $264,000 - $293,000.

The final salary offered to a successful candidate will be dependent on several factors that may include but are not limited to years of experience, skillset, geographic location, industry, education, etc. Base pay is one part of the Total Package that is provided to compensate and recognize employees for their work, and this role may be eligible for additional discretionary bonuses/incentives, and restricted stock units.

Pay range

$264,000—$293,000 USD

What We Can Offer You

Veracyte is a growing company that offers significant career opportunities if you are curious, driven, patient-oriented and aspire to help us build a great company. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, and are committed to fostering an inclusive workforce, where diverse backgrounds are represented, engaged, and empowered to drive innovative ideas and decisions. We are thrilled to be recognized as a 2024 Certified™ Great Place to Work® in both the US and Israel - a testament to our dynamic, inclusive, and inspiring workplace where passion meets purpose.

Veracyte (Nasdaq: VCYT) is a global diagnostics company whose vision is to transform cancer care for patients all over the world. We empower clinicians with the high-value insights they need to guide and assure patients at pivotal moments in the race to diagnose and treat cancer. Our Veracyte Diagnostics Platform delivers high-performing cancer tests that are fueled by broad genomic and clinical data, deep bioinformatic and AI capabilities, and a powerful evidence-generation engine, which ultimately drives durable reimbursement and guideline inclusion for our tests, along with new insights to support continued innovation and pipeline development. new_jobs.title: Director of Community Engagement, Alpha - $400,000/year USD
new_jobs.description:
Families who enroll at Alpha rarely arrive because of an advertisement. They come because someone they trust—another parent, across the table at dinner—told them, "This transformed my child." You would be responsible for that word-of-mouth engine across an entire region: orchestrating the dinners, cultivating parent ambassadors, engaging the mayor's office, connecting the CEO who gives a 14-year-old their first meaningful project.

In a typical week, you will be present in four different rooms. You design and execute the regional event calendar—gatherings that range from 150-person open houses to eight-seat curated dinners, several times each month. You identify and prepare current parents who are eager to speak with prospective families, then facilitate those family-to-family connections. You cultivate ties with civic leaders and corporate executives, converting those relationships into event venues, allies for campus expansions, and tangible opportunities for students. And you deliver the Alpha Networks promise: introductions, expert-led masterclasses, internships, alumni integration—tracked and fulfilled family by family.

There is no complete playbook waiting for you. You will build it as you execute, and the frameworks you create will be adopted by colleagues running parallel efforts in other markets. As your region expands, the performance bar rises rather than drops: doors opened per family must increase even as total enrollment grows. Success is measured by the proportion of new families who arrive through genuine personal endorsements, tracked over years rather than quarters.

No specific degree or institutional background is required. An MBA, a career in consulting or wealth management, or a track record built through community work, hospitality, or institutional advancement all carry equal weight. What matters is your demonstrated ability to convene people and convert those relationships into measurable outcomes.

This position is based on-site in one of the following regions: San Francisco, Los Angeles, San Diego, Denver, Greenwich, Miami, Atlanta, Boston, Oklahoma City, Tulsa, Dorado, Nashville, or Park City. The role involves evening and weekend engagements with high-expectation parents, elected officials, and entrepreneurs, along with consistent local travel. You will become the most connected individual in your city, and you will direct that capital toward children. If that exchange feels like the purpose rather than a burden, you should apply.

What You Will Be Doing

Creating and executing the regional event calendar: open events, curated dinners segmented by city and grade level, and family retreats—multiple events monthly, within budget
Identifying and securing venues, hosts, and vendors, then serving as the live host for each event
Identifying and training current parents to serve as ambassadors, arming them with authentic narratives, and pairing them with prospective families and campus tours
Establishing connections with government officials and corporate leaders, and converting those into event venues, support for new campus launches, and opportunities for students
Facilitating enrollment of families into parent circles and placement of students into mentorships, masterclasses, and professional internships; welcoming graduating families into the alumni network within 30 days
Recording every event, introduction, and first-contact source in the CRM to ensure "doors opened per family" is an accurate, verifiable metric

What You Won’t Be Doing

Purchasing growth. No paid advertising, no ad budgets, no targets based on impressions or lead volume
Controlling the brand narrative or executing top-down campaigns; that belongs to Marketing
Handling admissions processing, conducting tours, or managing enrollment documentation; Admissions and Family Success own those functions
Managing day-to-day campus operations or opening physical facilities
Treating raw attendance or headcount as if a full room alone constitutes success
Waiting for a complete playbook, templates, or dedicated support staff before taking action

Director Of Community Engagement Key Responsibilities

Drive people-first referrals to become the primary source of enrollment growth in your region.

Basic Requirements

5+ years building communities or relationship-driven programs in K-12 education, membership organizations, or comparable network businesses where growth originated from people: referrals, members, congregations, chapters, alumni, or client portfolios, with quantifiable results
Personal experience designing and executing 20+ events spanning the full spectrum, from intimate curated dinners to open events with 100+ attendees, including budget responsibility
Established and sustained relationships with government officials or corporate executives that delivered concrete, identifiable outcomes
Disciplined CRM practitioner; tracking relationships, attributions, and actions is already standard practice for you
Currently resides in, or willing to relocate to, one of these regions: San Francisco, Los Angeles, San Diego, Denver, Greenwich (CT), Miami, Atlanta, Boston, Oklahoma City, Tulsa, Dorado (PR), Nashville, or Park City (UT)
Authorized to work in the US without requiring visa sponsorship

Nice-to-have Requirements

Led regional growth, community, or partnership functions for a network-based organization: a school network, membership club, franchise system, or civic or faith-based institution
Developed and monetized a high-trust portfolio of relationships as a client-facing principal in wealth management, consulting, or business development
Advanced through admissions, institutional advancement, community organizing, or hospitality, and were consistently selected to host and represent the organization
Pre-existing relationships with local government or the business community in your target city
Deep understanding of how families evaluate and make high-stakes education decisions

About Alpha

Join the team building school around student growth

Alpha reimagines the school day around faster learning, stronger mentorship, and more time for students to build real-world skills.

Roles with real student impact:
Alpha hires teachers (guides), operators, admissions experts, school & curriculum leaders, and remote team members.

Education work that pays like it matters:
Alpha offers six-figure roles for people ready to help build a radically better school experience.

A culture built for builders:
Alpha is fast-moving, ambitious, and student focused. It’s for people who want to improve the system, not maintain it.

Alpha is where you can do the most meaningful work of your career.

There is so much to cover for this exciting role, and space here is limited. Hit the Apply button if you found this interesting and want to learn more. We look forward to meeting you!

Working with us

new_jobs.description:
Job Description

USF Advancement connects the university with donors who want to make a difference by providing philanthropic support to promote student success, research, academic excellence and other strategic priorities. With an endowment that now exceeds $700 million in value, our dedicated team of approximately 200 professionals, including 60 fundraisers, encompasses alumni, development and foundation operations. The team is responsible for raising more than $150 million annually and has broken records year after year with more than $184 million raised in fiscal year 2025.

The Director of Development is a fundraising professional responsible for securing philanthropic support for Women in Leadership & Philanthropy (WLP) and strategic priorities across the University of South Florida.

Reporting directly to the Assistant Vice President for Affinity Programs and Executive Director of Women in Leadership & Philanthropy, this position is dedicated exclusively to development activities and serves as a key member of the USF Advancement team.

The Director of Development identifies, qualifies, cultivates, solicits, and closes major gifts from individuals, corporations, and foundations. The successful candidate will manage a portfolio of prospects and donors, develop meaningful relationships that advance donor engagement, and partner with university leadership to align philanthropic investments with institutional priorities.

Employees of USF Advancement live out the values of responsibility, innovation, service, and excellence in each of its highly collaborative departments. We use trusted data and ethical AI to enhance decision-making, strengthen engagement, and enable our teams to focus on what matters most: relationships and impact.

This position is primarily onsite and requires flexibility to meet with donors and prospects throughout the Tampa Bay region and beyond.

Responsibilities

Identify, cultivate, solicit and manage a portfolio of major gift prospects and donors ($50,000+) with a focus on securing significant philanthropic support for Women in Leadership & Philanthropy and the University of South Florida.
Identify and qualify new prospects through research, referrals, volunteer engagement, and personal outreach.
Conduct discovery, cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship meetings with prospects and donors.
Develop and implement individualized strategies to move prospects through the donor pipeline from identification to gift commitment.
Collaborate with advancement colleagues and university stakeholders to identify philanthropic opportunities and align donor interests with institutional needs.
Prepare proposals, gift agreements and other donor communications that support fundraising objectives.
Maintain accurate records of prospect activity, strategy, and outcomes within university systems.
Meet established activity and fundraising goals, including visits, solicitations, proposal submissions, and gift commitments.
Represent the University of South Florida and Women in Leadership & Philanthropy at donor meetings, events, and community engagements as appropriate.
Perform other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

This position requires Bachelor's degree and 5 years of experience related to development or other appropriate professional experience. Five to seven years demonstrated experience identifying, cultivating, soliciting, and closing major ($50,000+) philanthropic gifts is preferred.

About Us

Working at USF

With approximately 16,000 employees, the University of South Florida is one of the largest employers in the Tampa Bay area. We are dedicated to cultivating a talented, engaged and driven workforce that strives to be bold. Employees excel in USF‘s rich academic environment, which fosters their development and advancement. In 2025, Forbes recognized USF as one of Florida’s best large employers, ranked No. 1 among the state’s 12 public universities. Our first-class benefits package includes medical, dental and life insurance plans, retirement plan options, employee and dependent tuition programs, generous leave, and hundreds of employee perks and discounts.

About USF

The University of South Florida is a top-ranked research university serving approximately 50,000 students from across the globe at campuses in Tampa, St. Petersburg, Sarasota-Manatee and USF Health. USF is recognized by U.S. News & World Report as a top 50 public university and the best value in Florida. U.S. News also ranks the USF Health Morsani College of Medicine as the No. 1 medical school in Florida and in the highest tier nationwide. USF is a member of the Association of American Universities (AAU), a group that includes only the top 3% of universities in the U.S. With an all-time high of $738 million in research funding in 2024 and as a top 20 public university for producing U.S. patents, USF uses innovation to transform lives and shape a better future. The university generates an annual economic impact of more than $6 billion. USF’s Division I athletics teams compete in the American Athletic Conference. Learn more at www.usf.edu .

Compliance and Federal Notices

new_jobs.title: Program Director
new_jobs.description:
Job Type

Full-time

Description

SGA provides a wide range of social services in some of Chicago's most challenged and consistently underserved communities and creates long-term and community-wide change.

Job Overview

SGA provides a wide range of social services in some of Chicago's most challenged and consistently underserved communities and creates long-term and community-wide change.

Major Duties And Responsibilities

Ensures all program deliverables meet per contract requirements and work closely with program staff to ensure timely outcome reports are being submitted.
Works closely with Program Coordinators/supervisors in overall performance of a multi-agency approach, including multiple partner agencies and community linkages.
Leads the identification of program updates required because of regulatory changes; responsible for documenting, training, and communicating key messages to the team.
Responsible for supervising program staff.
Ensures that all program services are of the highest quality.
Supervises, trains, and evaluates the performance of staff which includes coaching and program specific onboarding.
Maintains sound financial management of program budgets in assigned portfolios.
Manages departmental productivity standards.
Develop and enhance working relationships with community-based organizations, city, state, federal government agencies and partnered agencies as appropriate.
Collaborates with all levels of senior management in identifying additional funding sources and responding to requests for proposals.
Serves as a liaison between existing dedicated resources to promote shared learning and best practice identification and communication.
Understands data and articulates data needs required to assist with program needs; evaluates analytical outputs to test relevance and applicability and identify key insights.
Oversee the development and coordination of training seminars for staff and/or community partners.
If needed, develop, and implement an ongoing assessment/reassessment process for operational efficiencies, clients/families, coworkers, colleagues, and self.
Ensures all statutory and regulatory requirements are met, and all required licenses are up to date.
Ensure all department staff are trained regularly to meet compliance regulations.
Performs additional duties as assigned.

Requirements

KEY COMPETENCIES

Competent in Microsoft Office tools and inputting services into an online database.
Efforts to Outcomes data system.
Familiar with various screening tools.
Other duties as assigned

Requirements

Must have a strong work ethic.
Must be well organized and a self-starter
Detail-oriented, professional attitude, reliable.
Possess strong organizational and time management skills
Strong problem-solving skills, solid accounting principles knowledge, documentation skills, research, and resolution
Ability to communicate effectively and in writing, with staff and operational management.
Ability to work independently and with a team in a fast-paced environment with emphasis on accuracy and timeliness

Education

Master's degree (preferred) in public health administration with a focus on maternal health, social services, early childhood, or related field.

Experience

At least 5 to 7 years of extensive management experience, specifically overseeing multiple, complex programming.

Other

Experience in mental health, case management, and development of large facilities and/or multi-site preferred. Comprehensive knowledge of wraparound and comprehensive services. Significant experience in organizational/administrative development, program management with a demonstrated track record of success. A clear understanding of the community(s) being served. Demonstrated track record of strong community engagement skills. Sensitivity to cultural diversity is required. Ability to communicate and cooperate with diverse families, various professionals, and community groups. Has a thorough knowledge of community resources and services

Conditions of Employment

Ability to work varying hours Monday - Friday; schedule may include some evenings and weekends.
Office Software Proficiency: High proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint) or G Suite (Docs, Sheets, Slides).
Ability to travel between various work sites in Metropolitan Chicago

Physical Requirements

Must be able to remain stationary 50% of the time.
Must be able to frequently move inside the office to access file cabinets, office machinery, etc.
Occasionally ascends/descends stairs.
At times, it may be required to lift up to 25 lbs. for various needs
Frequently moves in outdoor weather conditions.

Benefits

FULL-TIME BENEFITS ELIGIBLE

Eligible employees receive a comprehensive benefits package that includes medical, dental, and vision insurance; employer-paid life insurance; short- and long-term disability coverage; a 403(b) retirement savings plan; paid vacation, sick leave, personal days, and holidays; an Employee Assistance Program; Benefits are provided in accordance with plan documents and organizational policies, and eligibility may vary based on employment status and scheduled hours.

Organizational policies and eligibility may vary based on employment status and scheduled hours.

Nothing in this job description restricts management’s right to assign or reassign duties and responsibilities to this job at any time; this description reflects management’s assignment of essential functions; it does not proscribe or restrict the tasks that may be assigned. This job description is subject to change at any time.

An Equal Opportunity Employer
